deposits.notes: The same URL is in forms/c710.json data_and_code.data_url (code_url is empty). Public without authentication. Recursive GitHub tree API https://api.github.com/repos/ctbaumler/personal_style_postedit/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1 returned HTTP 200, truncated=false, tree SHA 53a5d269292830011f33155dbdca3fdd035802d6. Exactly 82 files: README.md and 81 participant JSON logs; the files array lists README.md and the first 49 logs in path order, omitting 32 logs to respect the 50-file limit. README and all 81 logs were fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at this SHA and parsed in memory, each HTTP 200 and each below 20 MB; all byte lengths matched the API inventory. No analysis scripts, notebooks, embedding matrices, computed similarity scores, Pangram scores, CoLA scores, or LICENSE file appear in this complete tree or the inspected log schemas; README states no data license. Licenses for third-party models in the paper do not establish a license for this dataset. Each JSON object has one unique user_info.id matching its filename and six completed responses. Flattening responses and attaching user_info.id gives 486 completed output records: 324 with model_generation_shown=1 (post-editing) and 162 with model_generation_shown=0 (unassisted). Every participant has four treatment and two control outputs, and flags/scenarios agree with user_info.conditions/user_info.scenarios. All 486 have nonempty details, model_generation, and final_version. A model_generation is also stored for control tasks but was not shown; model_generation_shown determines exposure. The same 81 people contribute to both conditions. Block sequences among these analyzed records are 31 treatment-first [1,1,1,1,0,0] and 50 control-first [0,0,1,1,1,1]. Scenario-by-condition counts exactly match PDF Table 9. One log, logs/417a64ff-e3b5-45c1-a926-83e8b3897840.json, also contains responses['7'] with only start_time; this empty placeholder was excluded from rows_checked, which counts the 486 completed tasks, not 487 dictionary entries or 81 participant objects. has_outcome_scores=true refers to observed task-level self-report scores and workload ratings: edited-capture, edited-friend, edited-useable, and voice-important are populated for all 486 tasks; original-capture/original-friend/original-useable/original-content are populated for all 324 treatment tasks and null for the 162 controls. Numeric Likert responses are stored as strings. It does not mean that automated scores for screened outcomes S1-O1 through S1-O7 are deposited; those require rescoring the texts. No excluded/incomplete participant files, assignment-stage roster, allocation code, or S2 formative-survey records are present.

Public preregistration #253791, titled Post-Editing AI-Generated Text to Reflect One's True Voice, registered 2025-10-24 10:29 PT. The paper URL returns HTTP 200 HTML displaying the full preregistration; its Download PDF link also returned HTTP 200, a two-page 201453-byte PDF read in memory. n_files counts that preregistration document, not datasets. It describes within-person randomized block order, outcome definitions, exclusions, and planned analyses but contains no individual assignments or observed data. The planned recruitment target of 150 is not a realized randomized count. Question 5 specifies H1a-prime as a before-versus-after similarity change comparison, which clarifies the intended analysis but cannot confirm the inputs actually used for the published effect. No linked c710 data or analysis-code archive was provided on the preregistration page.

what_we_could_compute: final.open_items[0], partially: count the analyzed people and outputs by condition and recover their block sequences. Verified 81 unique people in both conditions, 324 post-edited and 162 unassisted final texts; 31 analyzed people completed treatment first and 50 control first. The analyzed logs cannot give the assignment-stage total, the randomization algorithm, or exclusion timing/reasons for absent participants.

final.open_items[1], partially: use participant IDs, task labels, condition flags, original drafts, and final texts to construct documented within-person and between-person comparisons, rescore LUAR-MUD/CISR similarities, calculate per-person means and across-person SDs/SEs by condition, and estimate diversity with uncertainty that preserves participant clusters and the within-person design. Scores and embeddings must be recomputed. Exact published reference aggregation, pair enumeration, test observation counts, bootstrap/permutation units, and mixed-model random effects cannot be recovered from these raw logs alone.

Directly calculate per-person and condition-level summaries, analyzed counts, SDs, SEs, and paired differences for deposited self-rated stylistic authenticity/usability and workload responses, and derive text lengths and edit measures. These self-report scores are distinct from the automated outcomes S1-O1 through S1-O7.

final.open_items[2], partially: reconstruct both final-level and change-score versions of H1a-prime after rescoring texts; the public preregistration specifies planned change scores. Without the authors' analysis script or labeled test inputs, the quantity actually standardized in the printed effect remains unconfirmed.

final.open_items[3-4] remain unresolved: texts allow a new acceptability analysis after establishing the CoLA checkpoint/settings, and voice-important supports new style-importance models, but the original CoLA subtraction order and Table 6 predictor coding cannot be inferred from the released logs. Historical CoLA/Pangram scores and the authors' fitted-model code are absent.
